strengths: Clearly identifies and addresses two concrete limitations of the SOTA F3Loc method: lack of uncertainty modeling and reliance on per-environment depth network training.

Extensive empirical evaluation across three datasets (synthetic Gibson, synthetic Structured3D, real-world LaMAR HGE/CAB) for both sequential and single-frame localization, with substantial reported improvements especially in the challenging real-world LaMAR setting (up to 16.7x recall improvement on short sequences).

Thorough ablation studies: uncertainty vs. no uncertainty, different pretrained monodepth encoders (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything V2 at multiple scales), grid resolution trade-offs, and observation-update frequency for runtime reduction.
Cross-domain generalization experiment (train on HGE, test on CAB) demonstrating that the pretrained-depth approach transfers better than F3Loc's custom-trained depth network.

Principled probabilistic formulation (Laplace observation model, NLL loss) that cleanly integrates uncertainty into the existing histogram-filter framework, with a clear description of how uncertainty propagates through the Bayesian update.
Efficiency analysis (accuracy vs. model size/runtime) showing favorable trade-offs even with smaller pretrained encoders.
Good qualitative visualizations (observation likelihoods, posterior evolution) that support the quantitative claims.
weaknesses: Methodological novelty is fairly incremental: the core architecture (masked attention, histogram filter) is directly inherited from F3Loc, and the two additions -- standard heteroscedastic Laplace uncertainty and swapping in an off-the-shelf pretrained depth encoder -- are individually well-established techniques rather than fundamentally new ideas.

On several single-frame localization metrics (Gibson(t), Structured3D), the uncertainty-aware variant is actually slightly worse than the non-uncertainty variant, and the explanation given (uncertainty only helps in sequential fusion) is plausible but not rigorously verified with additional analysis.

Test set sizes for LaMAR HGE at longer sequence lengths are quite small (e.g., N=11 for T=100, N=37 for Gibson), which limits the statistical robustness of the headline multiplicative improvement claims (2.7x, 16.7x).

In the cross-domain LaMAR CAB experiment, while success-rate (SR) numbers look strong, the underlying recall numbers in the supplementary (e.g., ~2.5% recall at 1m) reveal the absolute localization accuracy is still quite poor, suggesting the generalization claim is more nuanced than the main text implies.

The method incurs substantially higher per-frame runtime (up to ~1s on LaMAR) due to using a heavier pretrained depth network and matching step; while partially mitigated via grid coarsening and reduced observation frequency, this remains a practical drawback relative to F3Loc's lightweight custom network, and is somewhat downplayed in the main narrative.
Limited discussion of failure cases or sensitivity to gravity/intrinsics estimation errors (e.g., when GeoCalib is used instead of sensor data), despite this being a stated real-world use case.
Missing direct comparison to some other floorplan localization baselines (e.g., LaLaLoc++) on the same benchmarks; only LASER and PF-Net numbers are borrowed from prior work for a subset of datasets.

strengths: Addresses two concrete and well-motivated limitations of the state-of-the-art F3Loc method: lack of uncertainty modeling and the need for per-environment depth network training.
Extensive empirical evaluation across three datasets (synthetic Gibson, synthetic Structured3D, and real-world LaMAR HGE/CAB), covering both sequential and single-frame localization settings.

Large and consistent accuracy gains on the challenging real-world LaMAR dataset, including cross-building generalization experiments (HGE->CAB) that support the claim of improved out-of-the-box generalization.

Thorough ablations in the supplementary material (encoder choice, grid resolution, observation update frequency, fine-tuning on target domain) that help contextualize design choices and practical trade-offs.
Reasonably clear method description and useful qualitative visualizations (depth predictions, observation likelihoods, posterior evolution) that aid interpretability of the uncertainty mechanism.
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: the core contribution is largely a combination of existing, well-established components (F3Loc's histogram-filter pipeline, an off-the-shelf pretrained depth backbone, and a standard heteroscedastic Laplace NLL loss for aleatoric uncertainty), rather than a fundamentally new technique.

The benefit attributed specifically to uncertainty modeling is inconsistent: on Gibson(t) and Structured3D single-frame localization, uncertainty gives negligible or even slightly negative effects (e.g., MAE/cos-sim barely changes or worsens), and RMSE for successful sequences is sometimes worse with uncertainty than without (Table 1, T=100). This makes it hard to disentangle how much of the overall gain comes from uncertainty estimation versus simply swapping in a much stronger pretrained depth backbone.

The comparison baseline is essentially limited to F3Loc (with LASER/PF-Net numbers copied from F3Loc's paper for one dataset); no comparison is made against other recent uncertainty-estimation strategies (e.g., Gaussian NLL, ensembles, evidential/MC-dropout) or other floorplan localization approaches, limiting the ability to judge whether the specific uncertainty formulation is the best or merely adequate choice.

On LaMAR, F3Loc's depth network was retrained by the authors with limited in-domain data, while UnLoc leverages a backbone pretrained on vastly larger and more diverse external data (Depth Anything V2); the reported large improvement factors (2.7x, 16.7x) may partly reflect this pretraining-data asymmetry rather than purely the proposed uncertainty-aware fusion, and this confound is not fully disentangled.

Computational cost is noticeably higher for the proposed pipeline, particularly feature extraction time on Gibson (over 10x slower than F3Loc) and overall matching time on LaMAR, which could be a practical concern for latency-sensitive AR/robotics applications despite the paper's efficiency analysis arguing the trade-off is favorable.

The probabilistic/uncertainty formulation itself (Laplace likelihood with heteroscedastic scale, standard NLL training) is a fairly standard technique in depth/uncertainty literature, and the paper does not provide deeper theoretical justification or comparison to alternative uncertainty parameterizations.

strengths: Addresses two clear, well-motivated limitations of the prior SOTA (F3Loc): lack of uncertainty modeling in depth prediction and reliance on per-environment-trained depth networks.

Principled probabilistic formulation: modeling floorplan depth as a Laplace distribution with predicted scale (uncertainty) that is cleanly propagated into the observation likelihood and histogram filter update.
Leverages off-the-shelf pretrained monodepth models (Depth Anything V2) rather than custom per-dataset networks, which is a practically important contribution for generalization and deployment.

Extensive and convincing empirical evaluation across three diverse datasets (synthetic Gibson, synthetic Structured3D, and real-world LaMAR HGE/CAB), including both sequential and single-frame localization tasks.

Strong quantitative improvements, especially on the more realistic/challenging LaMAR dataset (2.7x and 16.7x recall improvements), with ablations isolating the contribution of uncertainty modeling vs. the pretrained encoder alone.

Good ablation studies: encoder choice (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything V2 variants at multiple sizes), efficiency analysis (model size/runtime vs. accuracy trade-offs), grid resolution, and observation update frequency.
Cross-dataset generalization experiment (train on HGE, test on CAB) with and without fine-tuning, showing the model transfers better than the baseline.
Qualitative visualizations (depth predictions with uncertainty bands, observation likelihood maps, posterior evolution) support and clarify the quantitative claims.

Reasonable reproducibility support: method is described in sufficient detail (equations for gravity alignment, masked attention, observation model, histogram filter, loss) and supplementary material gives training/dataset preprocessing details.
weaknesses: Novelty is somewhat incremental relative to F3Loc: the overall pipeline (gravity alignment, masked attention depth prediction, ray-based matching, histogram filter) is largely inherited from F3Loc, with the main technical additions being the Laplace uncertainty head and swapping in a pretrained encoder; the architectural/algorithmic novelty is modest.

The runtime cost is noticeably higher than F3Loc (especially matching time on LaMAR, ~0.88s vs F3Loc's much faster per-frame cost), which is a meaningful practical drawback only partially mitigated by coarser grids/less frequent updates in the supplementary.

On synthetic datasets where F3Loc's custom depth network can be trained effectively (Gibson, Structured3D), gains from uncertainty modeling are smaller and sometimes mixed (e.g., RMSE on successful sequences is worse for 'Ours w/ Uncertainties' than 'Ours w/o Uncertainties' or F3Loc fusion in Table 1), suggesting the benefit is concentrated in the harder real-world/out-of-domain regime.

The single-frame ablation shows uncertainty estimation provides little benefit outside LaMAR, raising the question of how much the headline gains are driven by the uncertainty mechanism itself versus simply using a stronger pretrained depth backbone.
Limited exploration of failure cases/limitations of the uncertainty model (e.g., calibration quality of predicted uncertainties is not directly validated beyond downstream localization numbers).

Comparison baselines are somewhat limited for the main sequential results (primarily F3Loc variants and LASER numbers copied from F3Loc paper); more recent floorplan localization methods or alternative uncertainty-aware approaches are not benchmarked.
The cross-domain generalization experiment (Table 3/7/8) uses very small test sets (N as low as 2 for T=100), limiting the statistical confidence of the generalization claims.

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing two clear limitations of the prior SOTA (F3Loc): lack of uncertainty modeling and per-dataset depth network training. The proposed solutions (Laplace-distributed uncertainty-aware depth prediction and off-the-shelf monodepth features) are simple, principled, and clearly explained.

Strong and comprehensive empirical results: large improvements over F3Loc on both synthetic (Gibson) and challenging real-world (LaMAR HGE, including the full uncropped scene) datasets, with especially dramatic gains on short sequences (42.2x SR improvement on 15-frame sequences), which is practically important for fast localization.

Extensive ablations: encoder choice (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything v2 at multiple sizes) with and without uncertainty, Laplace vs Gaussian uncertainty modeling, grid resolution vs runtime trade-offs, observation update frequency, single-frame vs sequential localization, and cross-domain generalization (HGE->CAB) with/without fine-tuning — providing thorough evidence for each design choice.

Good engineering/practical considerations: gravity alignment for handheld devices, lightweight uncertainty-weighted post-processing optimization, and runtime analysis showing the method remains near real-time.
Reasonably strong reproducibility statement with code, dataset preprocessing details, and training details provided in appendix.
The paper is honest about limitations, e.g., higher computational cost of off-the-shelf depth encoder, and provides mitigations (frame-skipping, coarser grid) with quantified trade-offs.
weaknesses: Novelty is somewhat incremental: the core architecture (masked attention, histogram filter, ray-based matching) is directly borrowed from F3Loc, with the main contributions being (a) swapping in a pretrained monodepth encoder and (b) adding an aleatoric uncertainty head with a standard Laplace/Gaussian NLL formulation, both of which are well-established techniques in other depth/localization contexts (e.g., Kendall & Gal 2017, Roessle et al. 2022).

The custom-constructed LaMAR HGE/CAB 2D floorplan ground truth relies on a manually calibrated affine transformation (4 doorway point pairs) with no independent ground-truth verification beyond qualitative consistency checks (residuals, raycast depth matching), which introduces some uncertainty into the reported real-world numbers.

Comparison to F3Loc on LaMAR uses a self-trained F3Loc model (since no official checkpoint exists for this dataset), which is reasonable but leaves open the possibility that F3Loc's poor performance partly reflects suboptimal retraining/hyperparameters rather than a fundamental limitation, especially given the very large performance gap (e.g., 0% success in Table 4).

Only one real-world building (LaMAR HGE/CAB, same underlying campus/dataset family) is used for real-world evaluation; broader real-world diversity (different buildings, sensor types, more heterogeneous conditions) would strengthen generalization claims.

Epistemic uncertainty is explicitly not modeled (acknowledged by the authors), which could matter more for true out-of-distribution/zero-shot floorplan generalization claims than the cross-domain LaMAR HGE->CAB experiment (which the authors themselves note is not a strict zero-shot setting since the same sensor/dataset family is used).

Runtime is meaningfully higher than F3Loc on LaMAR (~1s/frame due to depth encoder and matching), which is only partially mitigated by proposed tricks (frame skipping, coarser grid) and could limit real-time deployment on resource-constrained AR/mobile devices, a key motivating use case.

strengths: Clearly identifies and addresses two concrete limitations of the prior SOTA (F3Loc): lack of depth uncertainty modeling and reliance on per-environment-trained depth networks.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across synthetic (Gibson, Structured3D) and real-world (LaMAR HGE/CAB) datasets, with sequential and single-frame localization, ablations over multiple depth encoders (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything v2 at 3 sizes), uncertainty-distribution ablation (Laplace vs Gaussian), grid-resolution and observation-frequency studies for runtime/accuracy trade-offs, and an efficiency analysis relating model size/runtime to accuracy.

The Laplace-based aleatoric uncertainty formulation is simple, has closed-form likelihood for efficient real-time histogram filtering, and is used consistently both in the observation model and in a weighted post-processing optimization.
Reports large, consistent gains over F3Loc on the challenging real-world LaMAR HGE dataset, including on short sequences, which is practically relevant.
Reasonable reproducibility effort: training details, dataset construction procedure (including the LaMAR floorplan alignment methodology), and a code release are provided.
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: the aleatoric uncertainty formulation (Laplace/Gaussian NLL depth prediction) is a well-established technique (Nix & Weigend 1994; Kendall & Gal 2017; Roessle et al. 2022) applied to an existing pipeline (F3Loc's masked attention + histogram filter); the core architectural novelty is thus largely incremental/combinatorial rather than conceptually new.

Ablations (e.g., Table 5) suggest that a substantial portion of the reported gains over F3Loc come from simply swapping in a stronger pretrained depth encoder (Depth Anything v2) rather than from the proposed uncertainty modeling itself; the paper's framing sometimes attributes headline improvements broadly to 'UnLoc' without always isolating the uncertainty contribution clearly from the backbone-swap contribution.

The claim of removing the need for per-environment training is overstated: the masked-attention depth/uncertainty heads still require training on a given dataset's floorplan depth supervision, and the cross-dataset generalization experiments (LaMAR HGE → CAB) show that fine-tuning on target-domain data still yields notable additional gains (Tables 7–8), undermining the 'no retraining needed' narrative.

The headline multiplicative improvement numbers (e.g., 42.2x on short sequences) are computed relative to an extremely weak F3Loc baseline on LaMAR (near-zero success rates), which can be a misleading way to communicate significance; absolute performance numbers (e.g., 50.6% SR at T=15) are themselves still fairly low and should be emphasized alongside relative gains.

The ground-truth 2D pose/floorplan alignment procedure for LaMAR HGE/CAB relies on a manually fitted affine transform from only 4 point correspondences per scene, with no independent ground-truth validation of the resulting 2D poses — this raises some concern about the reliability of the evaluation protocol on the real-world datasets, which the paper only partially justifies via indirect consistency checks.

Evaluation remains restricted to indoor building floorplans similar to those used by the F3Loc benchmark; no entirely new environment types or sensor modalities are explored, limiting evidence of broader generalization claims.

The post-processing optimization is a somewhat ad hoc add-on (not deeply motivated or ablated beyond showing it helps) and incurs non-trivial extra runtime (~1s), which is not thoroughly contrasted against simpler alternatives.

Baseline comparison is narrow (mainly F3Loc and, for completeness, LASER); no comparison to other recent sequence-based or uncertainty-aware localization approaches, leaving the breadth of positioning relative to the wider literature somewhat thin.

strengths: Addresses two clear and well-motivated limitations of the prior SOTA method F3Loc: lack of uncertainty modeling in depth predictions and reliance on per-dataset-trained depth networks. The paper clearly articulates the problem and situates it within a thorough related-work discussion.

The proposed Laplace-distribution-based uncertainty formulation is simple, principled, and integrates naturally into both the histogram filter observation model and a novel uncertainty-weighted post-processing optimization, with efficient closed-form likelihood computation suitable for real-time filtering.

Leveraging off-the-shelf pre-trained monodepth models (Depth Anything v2) removes the need for costly per-environment depth network training, improving practical deployability and generalization, which is convincingly demonstrated via cross-building evaluation (HGE to CAB).

Extensive and rigorous empirical evaluation across synthetic (Gibson) and real-world (LaMAR HGE, cropped and full, CAB) datasets, with substantial improvements over F3Loc, including very large gains on short sequences (up to 42x) and long sequences (2.7x) on the challenging LaMAR HGE dataset.

Thorough ablation studies covering different monodepth encoders (DINOv2, DepthPro, Depth Anything v2 at multiple scales), Laplace vs Gaussian uncertainty modeling, grid resolution trade-offs, observation update frequency, and single-frame vs sequential localization, which convincingly isolate the contribution of each design choice.

Reasonable discussion of runtime/efficiency trade-offs (Fig. 4, Table 3) showing the uncertainty-aware approach is competitive even with smaller encoder variants, partially mitigating the added computational cost of using larger pre-trained models.
Reproducibility statement with code and detailed training/dataset construction details in the appendix, including transparent description of the LaMAR floorplan alignment procedure.
weaknesses: The novelty is somewhat incremental relative to F3Loc: the overall pipeline (gravity alignment, masked attention depth prediction, equiangular ray matching, histogram filter) is largely inherited, with the main new contributions being the Laplace uncertainty head and swapping in an off-the-shelf monodepth backbone. This could be viewed as a solid but relatively narrow extension rather than a fundamentally new approach.

The ground-truth 2D pose alignment for LaMAR HGE/CAB relies on a manually fit affine transformation from four doorway correspondences, which the authors admit lacks independent verification; given that the headline numbers (e.g., 42.2x improvement) are computed on this dataset, some residual uncertainty about the precision of the evaluation ground truth remains.

Only one strong baseline (F3Loc) is thoroughly compared against; other recent floorplan localization or depth-uncertainty approaches (e.g., LaLaLoc++, more recent uncertainty-aware depth fusion methods) are mentioned but not empirically compared, limiting the breadth of the competitive evaluation.

The runtime overhead of the off-the-shelf monodepth encoder is non-trivial (e.g., ~0.18s vs 0.015-0.09s for F3Loc's custom network on LaMAR), and while the paper argues lower frame rates are acceptable, this trade-off is not deeply analyzed in terms of practical real-time deployment constraints.

Epistemic uncertainty is explicitly left for future work, and the aleatoric-only formulation may still struggle in genuinely out-of-distribution scenes (e.g., very different building types) where epistemic uncertainty would be most useful; the generalization experiments (HGE to CAB) are not a strict zero-shot test as acknowledged by the authors.

The paper's narrative and ablations are dense with many tables, which, while thorough, could benefit from clearer synthesis/summary of which components matter most across settings, especially regarding interactions between uncertainty modeling and post-processing.
